title: Insights into the recruitment of the H3K4me3 reader Spp1 by the meiotic double-strand break protein Mer2.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the full metadata record and the raw scattering curve for SASDXW2 from the Small Angle Scattering Biological Data Bank (SASBDB): the file is 534 rows of three unlabelled numeric columns (scattering angle q, intensity I, error), ~24 kB. Metadata confirms it is one SEC-SAXS (size-exclusion-coupled small-angle X-ray scattering) measurement of one Mer2-Spp1 protein complex. The paper's data availability statement names exactly four such entries. Also read the open-access full text, methods and all supplementary-item mentions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Contents of Supplementary Tables S1-S6 (binding kinetics, SAXS collection parameters, plasmids, oligonucleotides, yeast strains, AlphaFold input sequences) - the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out twice, so the supplement itself is not retrievable and its contents are known only from the in-text captions. Atomic force microscopy force-distance curves, SEC-MALS (size-exclusion chromatography with multi-angle light scattering) masses, pulldown gels, condensate microscopy, Southern blots and spore-viability data are described in the text but not deposited anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: Verified: all four SASBDB entries download freely with no login; I retrieved SASDXW2's raw .dat and its full JSON metadata record. Supplementary tables are behind a timing-out Europe PMC endpoint but are in the published supplement.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Fail. There is no prediction target anywhere in the deposited data. The only files are raw X-ray scattering curves (angle, intensity, error); any machine-learning label - binding affinity, stoichiometry, interface residues - would have to be constructed by hand from figure panels and prose.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences for Mer2 (UniProt P21651) and Spp1 (UniProt Q03012) are present verbatim in the SASBDB metadata I downloaded, so inputs would not need lookups - but there is nothing to pair them with.

a4_units_stated.note: The .dat file itself has no header, but the SASBDB record states angular unit 1/Angstrom and intensity unit 1/cm, so units are recoverable.

a5_enough_rows.note: Fail, badly. Four deposited SAXS measurements of four protein-complex configurations. The per-curve 534 points are one physical measurement, not 534 examples. Checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.note: Four ~24 kB text files. Trivially fits, but there is nothing to fit.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper's data availability statement names four SASBDB identifiers; all four resolve and the one I opened matches the described Mer2-Spp1 complex and 4x2 stoichiometry.

a8_label_provenance.note: Fail. The paper's central structural claims are AlphaFold predictions (its own text calls them models requiring experimental validation), so any structure-derived label would be another model's output - the circularity case the checklist warns about.

integration.join_key: UniProt accession (P21651, Q03012) is present, but only two proteins carry it
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: two proteins joined to any large resource is a lookup, not a dataset.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: the deposited data is four biophysical measurements of one protein-protein complex, which is a structural result rather than a training set.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use two protein sequences to predict how many copies of each one assemble into a complex.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered was predicting binding stoichiometry and interface residues from protein sequence pairs. This paper supplies four examples (four measured Mer2-Spp1 complex configurations), which is roughly 400 times too few.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the number of copies of each protein in the complex. Here the true answer comes from small-angle X-ray scattering and light scattering on purified yeast proteins, both reported as 4 copies of Mer2 to 2 of Spp1.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Meiosis researchers would like to know which chromosome-axis proteins recruit which chromatin readers, but this paper's four measurements cannot train anything; its value is the biology, not the data.

ml_idea: None viable. The only conceivable task - predicting protein-complex stoichiometry or interaction-interface residues from sequence - would need a large curated set of measured stoichiometries (which exists elsewhere, e.g. in the Protein Data Bank and in published SEC-MALS compilations), not this paper's four complexes. This paper would at best contribute four rows to such a set.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the one file I actually downloaded (24 kB, 534 rows) times four deposited entries; no timing was run because there is no task to time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited data records: the data availability statement lists four SASBDB identifiers and nothing else. One minute, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Structural biology paper whose entire deposited dataset is four small-angle X-ray scattering curves of one protein complex. Fails A5 (four examples against the ~1,500 needed), A2 (no prediction target exists as a column; any label would be read off figures) and A8 (the structural claims are AlphaFold predictions, so a structure-derived label would just distil another model). Verified by downloading the raw scattering file and its metadata, not by reading the abstract. Excellent biology, no machine-learning project.
